description: A time-limited, approved departure from a requirement - a policy, a commitment, a control or a vulnerability SLA - for the things it names. An extension moves a deadline; an acceptance lets the departure stand until it expires. It covers its subjects only while approved, until expires. It names what it departs from (requirement or requirement_ref) and what it covers (subjects, subject_refs or scope, at least one).

examples.compensating: The vulnerable function is not reachable from request input; the WAF rule blocks the known payload.
examples.reason: The fix needs a major upgrade that conflicts with the December release freeze.
examples.title: Upgrade lodash in api after the Q4 freeze

compensating.description: What reduces the risk meanwhile, in Markdown.

expires.description: The last day it covers. For an extension, the new deadline.

id.description: Such as ex-2026-014, for references like exception:ex-2026-014.

kind.description: extension is still to be fixed, by expires; acceptance is not being fixed, and is reviewed by expires.

original_due.description: For an extension, the deadline it moves; before expires.

replaces.description: The exception this one renews or amends.

requirement.description: What it departs from, when that travels in the same bundle.

requirement_ref.description: What it departs from, when that travels elsewhere.

scope.description: What it covers, by name, when it is a class of things rather than a list, such as every repository in the legacy-billing group.

source_fields.description: The source's own fields that no field here covers, under the source's names. Readers keep it and don't interpret it. Never a personal value that a field here would label.

status.description: Whether it is in force also depends on expires.

subject_refs.description: What it covers, when they travel elsewhere.

subjects.description: What it covers, when they travel in the same bundle.

title: exception
